correctness.rationale: The half-central-angle equation gives an exact polynomial equation for \(t=(2r)^{-2}\). The congruence \(U_{p-1}(x)\equiv(x^2-1)^{(p-1)/2}\pmod p\) for \(p=769\) forces the coefficient divisibilities of \(P\). The constant term of \(Q\) has exact \(769\)-adic valuation \(2\), all degrees below \(384\) have valuation at least \(2\), degrees \(384\) through \(767\) have valuation at least \(1\), and the leading coefficient is a \(769\)-adic unit. Thus \(Q\) has one Newton-polygon slope \(-1/384\). The standard Newton-polygon/local-ramification argument forces every local irreducible factor degree to be divisible by \(384\), hence the global minimal degree of the geometric root is \(384\) or \(768\) and is not a power of two. value.rationale: The example targets the exact order singled out in the 2013 source as the first constructible-regular odd case beyond its computational reach. Although the 2015 paper later proved existence abstractly, it did so through limit and Hilbert-irreducibility arguments and did not expose concrete integer data. Consecutive side lengths \(768\) and \(769\) with an exact one-segment Newton polygon provide a compact reproducible benchmark for this historically distinguished case and an elementary certificate whose mathematical content is not a routine numerical recomputation.
